title: The Morning Brief: NFL cutdown day reshapes rosters; Djokovic falls at US Open
dek: The NFL's 53-man roster deadline on Sunday produced notable trades and one arrest that will shape opening-day depth charts. Djokovic's first-round exit at the US Open marked a historic departure from Flushing Meadows.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: August 30 was cutdown day across the NFL, with teams making final roster moves hours before the 6 p.m. ET deadline, while tennis and baseball pursued their own schedules into late August.
bottom_line: NFL cutdown day on August 30 produced trades, roster moves, and two significant arrests that will reshape opening-day depth and raise disciplinary questions for the Colts and Packers ahead of Week 1. Djokovic's first-round exit at the US Open on August 31 marked his first opening-round loss at a Grand Slam since 2006, while Aaron Donald ended a two-year retirement to sign with the Rams for the season ahead. Watch for the Colts' decision on Keenan Allen's status, the timeline for Jacobs' criminal case, Ohtani's return to the Dodgers mound, and when Scheffler closes the gap on Woods' major championship record.
body: The NFL's annual 53-man roster deadline arrived on Sunday with the customary shuffle of trades and exits that settle opening-day depth charts. The Chicago Bears sent defensive tackle Gervon Dexter, their 2023 second-round pick and last season's full-time starter, to the Atlanta Falcons for cornerback Clark Phillips and a fifth-round pick, according to the desk's reporting. The Buffalo Bills moved center Sedrick Van Pran-Granger to the Indianapolis Colts, sending a 2027 seventh-round pick and receiving a 2027 sixth-round pick in return. Both moves arrived hours before the 6 p.m. ET cutdown deadline, a familiar rhythm for teams balancing immediate needs against draft capital.

A second event on cutdown day carried sharper weight. Keenan Allen, the 34-year-old receiver who signed with the Colts on August 19, was arrested early Sunday morning on preliminary charges of driving while intoxicated and DWI endangering a person, both misdemeanors, according to police reporting cited by the desk. Allen's blood alcohol content measured 0.08 or more, per the Indianapolis Metro Police Department. The arrest occurred hours after he played in Saturday's preseason game against Detroit, where he caught one pass for 24 yards. The Colts' roster decision on Allen ahead of cutdown now carries legal exposure and potential disciplinary review from the league.

Elsewhere on the roster deadline, the Green Bay Packers' running back Josh Jacobs was placed on the commissioner's exempt list on Sunday, rendering him ineligible to play while facing misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property announced by the Brown County District Attorney on August 28. Jacobs will remain on paid leave until his criminal case resolves and the league issues any disciplinary ruling. The Odell Beckham Jr. story moved in the opposite direction: the 33-year-old receiver made the New York Giants' 53-man roster after sitting out all of 2025, reuniting with head coach John Harbaugh as the Giants build receiver depth around first-round pick Malik Nabers. The Red Sox activated outfielder Roman Anthony and shortstop Trevor Story from the injured list before Sunday's game against the Yankees, restoring both players to the roster after absences exceeding three months.

In baseball, the Cardinals placed second baseman JJ Wetherholt, a Rookie of the Year candidate, on the injured list before Sunday's series finale against the Pirates with right wrist tendinitis after he played through discomfort for weeks. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said Shohei Ohtani will not pitch Sunday and is "not 100%", extending the timeline for his return as a starter. Max Scherzer struck out 10 batters against the Mariners on August 30, passing Gaylord Perry for ninth place all-time in career strikeouts with 3,535.

In professional tennis, Novak Djokovic, ranked No. 5 and seeded fourth at the US Open, lost to Argentine Mariano Navone, ranked No. 49, in a five-set marathon on August 31 in his first opening-round loss at the tournament since 2006. The match lasted four hours and 36 minutes, and Djokovic acknowledged visible health struggles throughout. World No. 1 Jannik Sinner is absent from the tournament through injury; defending champion Carlos Alcaraz is making his return from a wrist injury.

On the college football calendar, North Carolina defeated TCU 15-10 in Ireland on August 30 in the 2026 season opener, a 34-point swing from the Tar Heels' 48-14 loss to the same opponent last year. Quarterback Billy Edwards Jr. made his UNC debut with 232 passing yards.

Aaron Donald, the eight-time All-Pro defensive tackle, signed a one-year, $20 million contract with the Los Angeles Rams on August 30, ending a two-year retirement. He reunites with newly acquired pass-rusher Myles Garrett. The Rams prepare for their September 10 season-opener in Melbourne, Australia; McVay offered no timeline for Donald's debut, saying the team will take readiness one day at a time.

In golf, Scottie Scheffler won the 2026 Tour Championship at East Lake with a 16-under score, capturing his second FedEx Cup and surpassing Tiger Woods' all-time PGA Tour career earnings record. Scheffler's career total reached $130.39 million, exceeding Woods' 25-year-old record of $120.9 million by $9.49 million.

The NFL and NFLPA continue active negotiations over terms for player participation in flag football at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Central questions include injury insurance, salary-cap treatment for injured players, scheduling conflicts, and participation limits, with more than 200 NFL players having expressed interest and star quarterbacks Josh Allen and Joe Burrow publicly noted as considering competition.
